WAIT concerns replica memory, while WAITAOF requires observed local and replica AOF counts; neither subset establishes loss-free failover or a power-loss guarantee from this process-crash experiment. metrics.methodology: Latencies use 512 bounded geometric histogram buckets, starting at 1 microsecond and increasing by 5%; quantiles are nearest-rank bucket upper bounds. The last bucket covers the remaining duration range. All terminal client attempts, successful attempts, and failed attempts have separate histograms. Throughput is completed attempts divided by phase wall-clock seconds. Operations are attributed to the phase in which they start. Redirect counts include only terminal MOVED/ASK errors; redirects handled by the client are not observable here.

write_stages.methodology: Diagnostic SET, WAIT and WAITAOF stages are excluded from logical request and pacing counts. SET latency includes routing, pool/connection initialization and handled redirections before its terminal result; WAIT/WAITAOF latency covers only that attempted command on the same physical connection. Logical set_wait/set_waitaof latency covers the complete write executor operation. Short WAIT or WAITAOF replies have distinct wait_short/waitaof_short classes, separate from client timeout. Unissued commands have no stage latency. Reply histograms exclude errors and malformed replies; WAITAOF histogram keys are canonical local/replicas integer pairs. WAIT replica-memory acknowledgements and WAITAOF local/replica AOF acknowledgements remain separate. workload_stats.pacing_methodology: Offered requests are ideal period slots from workload Start until the dispatcher observes Stop or parent cancellation; the first slot occurs after one period. The period is one second divided by the configured aggregate rate, truncated to whole nanoseconds. A central dispatcher offers only the latest due slot over an unbuffered channel; missed slots, busy workers, stopped tokens, and tokens with no eligible operation are dropped, without catch-up requests. Started requests count actual logical workload GET or write executions; a SET+WAIT/WAITAOF write counts once. Completed requests count their terminal logical metrics attempts. After Stop, offered = started + dropped and started = completed. Validation and ordinary/acknowledgement-policy probes are excluded. These global counters are not attributed to phases.
workload_stats.guarantee: Every successful client SET acknowledgement is validated, including writes whose subsequent WAIT or WAITAOF returned too few acknowledgements or an error. Every write uses a unique immutable key. SET errors are ambiguous outcomes and may have executed; they are excluded from the acknowledged-write guarantee. WAIT-satisfied and WAITAOF-satisfied subsets are reported separately. WAIT concerns replica memory, while WAITAOF requires observed local and replica AOF counts; neither subset establishes loss-free failover or a power-loss guarantee from this process-crash experiment. Redis asynchronous replication can lose acknowledged writes during failover. This check establishes observed post-experiment readability and value equality, not a general durability guarantee.

methodology: Quiet administrative process, CONFIG, persistence INFO, keyspace and bounded data-file preparation occurs before baseline traffic; it issues no SAVE, BGSAVE, BGREWRITEAOF or explicit durability barrier.

The workload fully stops and joins in-flight acknowledgements before freezing its immutable ledger and counters. All later topology observations are read-only until every frozen acknowledged value has been checked. SET-error outcomes remain ambiguous, excluded from acknowledgement guarantees.

Original replicas are SIGKILLed before original primaries. Every fixed owned container must produce ErrProcessStopped administrative evidence with restart policy no before any restart. Original primaries restart before replicas in the same containers and retained volumes; original Redis Cluster identities and slot ownership must survive.

The model is sequential process SIGKILL while Docker VM, host and storage remain running, followed by same-container starts. It does not simulate power loss, host/page-cache loss or disk loss. Drain, kill and inspection intervals are reported because they permit background fsync progress.

Topology restoration requires all six original identities, endpoints, primary slot owners and replica assignments synchronized for stable_for, without forced Redis topology commands. Physical receipts retain early raw evidence, which can be transient during full sync. Six fresh quiet administrative runtime/configuration/file observations after topology stability prove the final persistence mode on those same restarted processes, within the shared repair budget and before frozen-value validation. Samples crossing restoration or diagnostic deadlines are retained but excluded from successful milestones.

Frozen-ledger GET validation happens exactly once before diagnostic SET/GET or configured replica-acknowledgement probes. Process/slot readiness and later diagnostic service are independent from frozen-value preservation; missing or corrupt values retain a partial data verdict even after service recovers.

Memory mode has RDB/AOF disabled, rdb-del-sync-files=yes to remove replication-created RDB files, and observed absence of value persistence files. Its persistence-recovery event is not applicable and remains absent; its independent persistence dimension is false. AOF modes use the RDB base preamble required by the pinned image's bundled modules plus incremental AOF records. AOF recovery requires actual matching healthy runtime configuration, loading=0 and complete frozen acknowledged-value preservation; this observation establishes no loss-free or power-loss guarantee.

No workload demand is offered after draining, so absent fault/recovery traffic does not measure zero availability or throughput. Post-validation probes are separate diagnostics and never enter workload metrics or the frozen ledger. Poll intervals follow sample completion; observations are sampled and non-atomic.

All AOF modes and write policies use six-node quiet runtime preparation followed by exactly three all-shard policy SET/GET warmup writes before baseline starts. Warmup writes are excluded from the workload ledger and metrics; no WAITAOF compatibility command is issued after baseline to alter crash-trial durability.
